framing.header: u16 id, u16 size, u16 idx - little-endian, 6 bytes, then `size` body bytes
framing.idx: sender sequence (seq & 0xFF) << 8, +1 per packet; server only logs gaps (net.lua check_is_record_xy)
framing.encryption: none on the stream; only CLAskLogin.encrypted_data is encrypted
framing.dispatch: net.lua register_packets: packets[xy_id] = table, iterated with pairs() -> if two live tables share an id the winner is undefined

wire.string_charset: client_wire_encoding = utf8 (confs/publish_yu/server_conf.lua); outgoing strings go through wire_charset.fromutf8 (identity + wire_names_vi translation)
wire.fixed_strings: bytes[N]: bostream.write(s, N) cuts at a UTF-8 boundary and pads with NUL; readers keep all N bytes (cut at the first NUL when used as text)
wire.writer_clamps: writeshort clamps to [-32768, 32767], writeushort to [0, 65535]; writeuint/writeint raise if the value does not fit (string.pack)

types.bytes[]: variable bytes; length from len_field (an earlier field) or len_expr (len_on_wire: false = length not on the wire)
types.str8/str16/str32: u8/u16/u32 byte count followed by that many bytes; len_name = name of the count field in the Lua code; guard = condition under which the bytes are read; min/max = limits implied by the guard
types.array<T> / kind: array: repeated element: count (constant), count_field (earlier field) or count_expr (count_on_wire: false = not on the wire); min/max from guards
types.struct X: nested struct, layout in structs: (codec bis or bos)
types.kind: blob: sub-stream serialized separately and embedded behind a len_type byte count
types.kind: if: branches evaluated in order; `when` uses the condition syntax below
types.kind: opaque: stream operation the extractor could not analyse (see note/error)

conditions: C-like: == != < <= > >= && || ! & | ^(xor) ~(bnot) << >> + - * / // %; #x = byte length of a string / element count of an array; names are earlier fields (current array element first, then outer scopes); name[i] = element i of another array indexed by the current loop; $name = server-side local that is not on the wire; math.floor(...) etc. keep Lua semantics

dsl.table: packet.<Name> = { xy_id = packet.XYID_<...>, new, ctor, bis, bos, [helpers], [constants] } inside M.bind(packet, bistream, bostream, gbk, define) of each packet_types/*.lua and packet_domains/*.lua file (login: top level of services/login/packet.lua)
dsl.bis(self, buffer): decoder used by the server for packets it RECEIVES (CG/CL/CGW): local stream = bistream.new(); stream:attach(buffer); self.f = stream:readT() ...
dsl.bos(self): encoder used by the server for packets it SENDS (GC/LC/WGC): local stream = bostream.new(); stream:writeT(self.f) ...; return stream:get()
dsl.struct codecs: types/*.lua: bis(self, stream) / bos(self, stream) work on the caller stream; called as packet.X.bos(obj, stream) or obj:bis(stream) after obj = packet.X.new()
dsl.primitives: read/write + uchar(u8) char(i8) ushort(u16) short(i16) uint(u32) int(i32) float(f32) ulong(u64) bool; read(n)/write(s, n) = n raw bytes; writeff(n) = n x 0xFF
dsl.arrays: for i = 1, N do ... end (N constant or earlier field), for _, v in ipairs(t) (count = #t written before), while-true loops with i = i + 1 / if i > N then return end
dsl.conditions: if/elseif/else on earlier fields; early `return` ends the packet
dsl.strings: u8/u16/u32 length + read(len) (-> strN); fixed read(0x1E)/write(s, 0x1E) (-> bytes[N])
dsl.helpers: self:read_x(stream)/self:write_x(stream, v) methods of the same table are inlined (fields carry `via`)
dsl.blobs: local inner = bostream.new() ... stream:writeint(#inner:get()); stream:write(inner:get(), n)
dsl.ids: services/game/packet_ids.lua (generated by split_packet.py, which is not on the server) and packet.XYID_* at the top of services/login/packet.lua

packets.name: GCCharBaseAttrib
packets.annotation: Conditions test the server-side m_uFlags[1..11]. On the wire they are new_flags[1..14] (combat.lua bos): new_flags[1] = m_uFlags[1] & 0x7F; for i = 2..11 new_flags[i] = (m_uFlags[i] << 1 | carry) & 0xFF with carry = previous byte >> 7 (first carry = m_uFlags[1] >> 7); new_flags[12] = last carry; new_flags[13..14] = DFeng flags. Receiver: m_uFlags[1] = (nf[1] & 0x7F) | (nf[2] & 1) << 7; m_uFlags[i] = nf[i] >> 1 | (nf[i+1] & 1) << 7.

packets.name: GCDetailAttrib_Pet
packets.annotation: Conditions test the server-side m_Flags[1..11]; the wire carries 12 remapped bytes _nf (pet_detail_types.lua bos, lines 791-810): new bits 0-1 = old 0-1, 3-8 = old 2-7, 9/10 = hp/hp_max mirrors (old 8/9), 11/12 = _has_rage/_has_rage_max, 90 = elf data, 13.. = old 10... The optional tail (GCStallPetView_t / GCExchangePetView_t, line 1035) is written only when the server attached extra_data; nothing on the wire announces it, the receiver can only tell from the remaining body length.
